subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — pricing and $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@fintechx.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Unit economics call — follow-up

Marissa / team — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and asks from our side so we can align internal stakeholders: 

- Expected monthly token volumes (rough):
  - Search & ranking: ~8–12M tokens/mo
  - Summarization (user transcripts): ~40–60M tokens/mo
  - Assist/chat features (context + responses): ~15–25M tokens/mo
  - Total run-rate: ~65–90M tokens/mo (starting POC around 25–35M)

- Budget / target pricing: our finance team is looking for unit costs in the range of $200–$300 per 1M tokens for initial procurement (this includes any SLA/enterprise uplift). They are open to commitments that lower that over time.

- Asks: could you share a simple workbook with per-feature $/1M scenarios and a baseline inference cost per 1M tokens (infrastructure + ops)? Also want a quick calc for CAC payback if we model a $/feature revenue line.

If you can send that over by Wednesday we’ll schedule a follow-up with finance and infra owners.

Thanks —
Raj
VP Product, FintechX
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics call — follow-up

Raj — great to meet, thanks for the clear numbers. Attaching a concise workbook (see attachment) and a pricing sheet that shows committed vs. on-demand tiers. High-level notes below so your finance team has context before we walk through the workbook: 

1) Baseline inference cost we use for modeling (infrastructure + ops, amortized GPU + network + support): ~ $20 per 1M tokens for the model family you described on a dedicated/enterprise SLA profile. 

2) Typical pricing guidance (starting points):
   - On-demand / hosted (no commit, SLA standard): $220–$300 per 1M tokens
   - Committed (12 month reserve, Dedicated pools): $100–$140 per 1M tokens (volume & term dependent)
   - Private / on-prem (customer infra): pricing shifts to platform fee + smaller per-token metering; we'll model that separately if needed.

3) Margin math and example feature-level calc (all shown in the attached workbook, excerpted below):
   - Assumptions: cost = $20 / 1M tokens; price = $120 / 1M tokens (committed scenario)
   - Gross margin = (price - cost) / price = (120 - 20) / 120 = 83%

   - Example feature: Summarization (50M tokens/mo)
     - Rev/mo = (50 / 1) * $120 = $6,000
     - Infra cost/mo = (50 / 1) * $20 = $1,000
     - Gross margin/mo = $5,000 (83%)

   - Example feature: Assist/chat (20M tokens/mo)
     - Rev/mo = 20 * $120 = $2,400; cost = 20 * $20 = $400; gross margin = $2,000 (83%)

4) CAC / payback example (illustrative):
   - If expected ARR per customer (committed) = $72k (6k/mo), and gross margin = 83%, gross margin dollars = $4,980/mo
   - With CAC = $25k (typical enterprise procurement + pilot + AE), payback = 25k / 4.98k ≈ 5 months
   - For smaller deals (POC-first): CAC effectively lower per revenue, payback can be 8–12 months depending on uplift to committed.

5) Key levers to improve price-to-cost ratio for you: longer commitments, model/quantization tradeoffs (reduce cost to ~$12–$15 per 1M for quantized runtime), and batching/caching on prefix-heavy workflows.

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll send the workbook (attached) with a few rows filled in for your reported volumes.
- Schedule a 60-min unit-econ deep-dive with finance + infra (Aditya + Dev on our side) — propose Thu 2026-07-01 10:00 PT (see Calendly link).

Attachment note: unit_econ_workbook_fintechx.xlsx (sample rows populated) and redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechx.com>

Subject: Re: Unit economics call — follow-up

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we sync with finance: 

1) The $20 / 1M tokens baseline — is that for your dedicated GPU pools with standard SLA? Does that include caching savings or is that pure per-token compute/network?
2) On the $100–$140 committed range: what volume thresholds did you assume (1M / 10M / 50M brackets)?
3) For CAC payback — can you show a conservative scenario (lower uplift to committed, smaller initial ARR) so our CFO can see the downside?

We will review the workbook and confirm the Thu 7/1 slot or propose an alternate. Please include the conservative row and list of model variants that give the $12–$15 cost floor you mentioned.

—Raj
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics call — follow-up

Raj — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and I attached an extra sheet with conservative scenarios.

1) $20 / 1M tokens baseline: this is our modeled fully-burdened cost on Dedicated GPU pools with standard support & network; it assumes typical prefix cache miss rates and moderate batching (what we use internally for production). Caching can reduce marginal cost per 1M significantly for repeat prompts; the $12–$15 floor is reachable when using quantized runtimes + aggressive KV/prefix caching and higher batch sizes.

2) Committed tiers (examples we put in the pricing sheet):
   - 1–10M tokens/mo: $140–$160 per 1M (12mo commit)
   - 10–50M tokens/mo: $110–$130 per 1M
   - 50M+ tokens/mo: $90–$110 per 1M (highest volume & term)
   Note: these ranges include a small enterprise SLA uplift; we can tighten once we agree on token mix and rollout timing.

3) Conservative CAC/payback sheet: we included a row that assumes a $12k CAC and an initial committed ARR of $18k (1.5k/mo), margin 70% (price assumed $100 /1M), payback ~8 months. That should give your CFO a downside view.

Next: I attached the workbook with both optimistic and conservative rows and a short model of $/feature monthly revenue + inference cost. I’m available Thu 7/1 10:00 PT — booking link: https://calendly.com/marissa-cole/unit-econ-deep-dive. If that works I’ll set the invite and loop in Aditya + Dev.

Attachments: unit_econ_workbook_fintechx.xlsx, redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
